mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a single month leads to a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financing conditions affecting corporate investment and consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a single month
regime_hint: Rising Fed Funds rate surprise in a restrictive policy regime
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the same month of the Fed Funds shock (t-test p > 0.05), or subsequent months see continued high corporate credit spreads without reversal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 4.5% for three consecutive months is associated with a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as rising labor market rigidity reduces consumer wealth and corporate hiring intentions.
regime_hint: Rising unemployment rate in a tightening labor market
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive during the UNRATE expansion phase (t-test p < 0.05), or the effect dissipates within 2 months of the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both HOUST (industrial production) and PAYEMS (employment) by at least 2% signals a demand shock, which predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as market anticipates a rebound in economic activity.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < previous month AND PAYEMS < previous month by ≥2%
regime_hint: Concurrent demand and supply contraction in a recessionary recovery
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the dual contraction (t-test p > 0.05), or the pattern persists for >3 months without SPX appreciation.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in INDPRO above 2% followed by a subsequent rise back to trend predicts a positive S&P 60-day forward return as the market anticipates normalization in supply chain constraints and improved production capacity.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >2% in a month and recovers to the prior month's level in the following month
regime_hint: Supply chain disruption easing in a growth-oriented regime
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain flat or negative during the recovery window (rolling IC < 0.05), or INDPRO never returns to pre-shock trend.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.5% in a single month during a period of stable FEDFUNDS, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to expectations of future inflation and tighter policy.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses up >0.5% while FEDFUNDS remains below 5.0%
regime_hint: High-inflation surprise in a low-rate environment
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative after controlling for inflation expectations (F-stat < 1.0), or CPIAUCSL reverts without policy tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in PAYEMS of at least 3,000 jobs for two consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 5-day forward return as market anticipates a weakening labor market and potential rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month AND PAYEMS < previous-to-previous month by ≥3,000
regime_hint: Labor market weakening in a tightening policy environment
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the jobless trend (t-test p > 0.05), or the decline reverses within 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly convergence of GDPC1 (GDP personal consumption) above trend and a simultaneous drop in RSAFS (retail sales) by 5% signals a demand-led cycle shift, predicting a positive S&P 20-day forward return as markets price in consumption-driven recovery.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > trend AND RSAFS falls > -5% in the same month
regime_hint: Demand recovery in a supply-constrained environment
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive during the convergence (IC < 0.05), or RSAFS recovers before GDPC1 stabilizes.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months in a low-inflation regime, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be positive as easing labor market conditions support corporate hiring and consumer confidence.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% for 2 consecutive months and inflation (CPIAUCSL) < 250
regime_hint: Labor market easing in a disinflationary environment
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain flat or negative despite UNRATE easing (rolling IC > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL rises unexpectedly.
